title: The verifier runs migrations on a disposable PostgreSQL and always tears it down
description:
SPIDR child 2 of task-8f86e10504c74e248ccfa6f427b41a15 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 task-463f195efd2f4fd2886790029a474194 for the `db:migrate` script it detects.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the verifier's DATABASE leg. When a workspace declares `db:migrate`, start a disposable PostgreSQL container on a random port, export DATABASE_URL to the recipe, run the migrations, THEN the tests, then tear the container down ON EVERY EXIT PATH. No deploy, no UI.

THE CONTAINER TEARDOWN IS THE SUBJECT, exactly as the preview runner's process cleanup was. A leaked container holds its port and its disk; the next verification then fails to bind and the failure appears far from its cause. The parent's DoD 1 requires the container gone after ACCEPT, after REJECT, AND after a forced kill - assert by asking DOCKER whether the container exists, never by an internal flag.

DOCKER ABSENT REFUSES, NEVER SKIPS. `MIGRATION_DB_UNAVAILABLE` with its layer, recorded as a refusal with a reason - the parent is explicit that the verifier NEVER SILENTLY SKIPS. A silent skip would let a node pass verification on a machine without docker while its migrations were never run, which is the worst outcome available here: a green node whose schema change was never executed.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb: the verifier runs the node's `test` recipe in the workspace with NO database (apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/node-verifier.ts, 230 lines; verifier-process-runner.ts, 395 lines). verifier-process-runner already has exactly the machinery this row needs and must reuse: injectable `spawn`, `timeoutMs`, `killGraceMs` and `killProcessGroup` (options at :49-55), a process-GROUP SIGKILL at :187-189, and timer cleanup on every exit path (:110-114). Read it before writing a container lifecycle - the shape of 'always clean up' is already solved there for processes.

ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING: migrations run BEFORE the tests. A test suite that runs against an unmigrated schema fails for a reason that looks like a product bug.
definitionOfDone: With a workspace declaring `db:migrate`, the verifier starts a disposable PostgreSQL on a RANDOM port, and the test proves DATABASE_URL REACHED THE RECIPE - assert from the recipe's own output or environment, not from the daemon's intent.

MIGRATIONS RAN BEFORE THE TESTS: assert the ordering observably (the migrated table exists at the moment the test recipe starts, or the recipe's output shows the migration first). A suite running against an unmigrated schema fails looking like a product bug.

THE CONTAINER IS GONE after ACCEPT, after REJECT, and after a FORCED KILL - three arms, each asserted by asking DOCKER whether the container exists, never by an internal flag. A leaked container holds its port and the NEXT verification fails to bind, far from the cause.

DOCKER ABSENT REFUSES MIGRATION_DB_UNAVAILABLE with its layer and is RECORDED AS A REFUSAL WITH A REASON - never a silent skip and never a pass. Assert the node does NOT reach ACCEPTED on that path: a green node whose migrations never ran is the worst outcome this row can produce.
MIGRATION_FAILED carries THE FAILING FILE (code + layer asserted): a migration failure that does not name which migration failed sends a seat to read all of them.

The random port genuinely avoids collision: two disposable databases can exist concurrently without one taking the other's port - assert with two simultaneous verifications, since parallel node staffing (task-92d84d38) makes concurrent verification the normal case, not an edge case.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: TEARDOWN ON EVERY EXIT PATH, asserted against DOCKER rather than a flag. A flag proves the code believed it cleaned up.
NEVER SILENTLY SKIP THE DATABASE LEG. Docker absent is a refusal with a code; a skip would let a node pass verification with its migrations unrun.

REUSE verifier-process-runner.ts's lifecycle discipline (injectable spawn/timeout/killGrace, process-group kill, cleanup on every path). A second independently-written lifecycle is how one of them leaks.
MIGRATIONS BEFORE TESTS, always, and provably.
CONCURRENT VERIFICATIONS ARE NORMAL now that nodes staff in parallel - the port strategy must survive two at once.

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE, AND NOTE THE SEAM THAT KEEPS THIS ROW OUT OF A CAP COLLISION. NO EDITS. (a) CONFIRM THE PREREQUISITE. task-463f195e ships the scaffold's `db:migrate` / `db:migrate:down` scripts this row detects. Prove it at the tree - the generated package.json template under `apps/daemon/src/repository/controlled-profile/` must declare both - and read its completionSummary from epicSiblings for the pinned tool and, critically, for its answer to whether `db:migrate:down` reverts ONE migration or ALL. If absent, moe.report_blocked with blockedOnTaskIds ['task-463f195efd2f4fd2886790029a474194'] and stop. (b) THE SEAM IS `runTest`, AND IT IS AN INJECTED FUNCTION - WHICH IS WHY THIS ROW NEED NOT TOUCH THE RUNNER AT ALL. `node-verifier.ts:58-59` declares `readonly runTest: (brief: NodeMission) => Promise<VerifierRunCapture>` ("Runs the spec's test in its workspace; injectable for tests"), called at :180. Production supplies it at ONE place: `agent-wrapper-main.ts:318`, `runTest: verifierRunner`. So the database leg is a WRAPPER around that function - start the container, export DATABASE_URL, migrate, delegate to the inner runTest, tear down - composed at :318. THAT MATTERS BEYOND elegance: `verifier-process-runner.ts` is 395 LINES AGAINST A 400 CAP, and a SIBLING ROW (task-945bb541, environment values into spawns) also needs that file. Two rows adding to five lines of headroom breaks it for whoever lands second. Wrapping `runTest` means this row adds ZERO lines there. If you find yourself editing verifier-process-runner.ts, stop and re-read this. (c) READ THE LIFECYCLE DISCIPLINE YOU ARE MIRRORING (rail 3) - do not write a second one from scratch: injectable `spawn`, `timeoutMs`, `killGraceMs`, `killProcessGroup`, `platform` (options :45-56); a single `cleanup()` that clears EVERY timer and kills the helper, called on every exit path (:105-118); best-effort process-group SIGKILL with the win32 case handled explicitly (:183-190). The container lifecycle wants the same shape: one teardown function, called on every path, injectable for tests. (d) NO DOCKER PRECEDENT EXISTS: `git grep -rn '"docker"' -- apps/daemon/src` outside tests returns NOTHING, so you are writing the first docker port in the daemon. task-c0e00f0a (the deploy engine) is writing another one concurrently for its own spawns - check whether it has landed and, if it has, reuse its port rather than minting a second docker invocation shape; if it has not, keep yours small and say so, because one of you will end up the precedent. (e) BASELINE (global rail 3), standalone foreground, quoting each count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. (f) `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/` and note peer dirt.

THE DISPOSABLE DATABASE, IN ITS OWN MODULE. NEW FILE `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/verifier-database.ts` plus its `.js` bridge (the orchestrator directory pairs every module with one; a missing bridge kills the daemon at boot with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND). It owns: detect, start, migrate, tear down. LET DOCKER CHOOSE THE PORT - THIS IS THE ONE DESIGN DECISION IN THE ROW AND THE OBVIOUS APPROACH IS RACY. Picking a free port in Node and passing `-p <chosen>:5432` has a TOCTOU window: the port is free when you look and taken when docker binds, and DoD-6 makes concurrent verifications the normal case, so that race is not hypothetical. Publish with `-p 0:5432` and read the assigned port back with `docker port <container> 5432` - docker binds first and tells you after, so there is no window. State that choice in the module docblock so the next reader does not 'simplify' it back into a race. NAME THE CONTAINER UNIQUELY per verification (the node ref plus a random suffix) so two concurrent runs cannot collide on a name either, and so the teardown arms can ask docker about a specific container rather than about 'the' container. WAIT FOR READY, DO NOT SLEEP: postgres accepts TCP before it accepts queries. Poll `pg_isready` (or an equivalent the image ships) until it answers or a bounded budget expires, and refuse on expiry rather than proceeding to a migration that will fail confusingly. ONE TEARDOWN FUNCTION, CALLED ON EVERY PATH, mirroring the runner's `cleanup()` shape - and it must be safe to call twice, because the forced-kill arm will. Spawn `docker` as a bare executable under `shell: false` with an ARGV ARRAY - never a shell string, never a chain. Take `spawn` injectable, exactly as the process runner does, so the tests in step 4 can drive every branch without a real daemon.

WRAP `runTest`, AND KEEP THE ORDERING PROVABLE. Compose the database leg around the injected `runTest` at `agent-wrapper-main.ts:318`. THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING (rail 4): detect `db:migrate` in the workspace's package.json; if absent, delegate straight to the inner `runTest` and change nothing - a workspace with no database must behave EXACTLY as today, and that is an arm in step 4. If present: start the container, wait for ready, run the migrations, and ONLY THEN call the inner `runTest` with `DATABASE_URL` in its environment. A test suite that runs against an unmigrated schema fails for a reason that looks like a product bug, which is why DoD-2 wants the ordering asserted OBSERVABLY rather than by reading the code. DATABASE_URL REACHES THE RECIPE THROUGH THE RUNNER'S ENVIRONMENT OPTION, and note what that means: `verifier-process-runner.ts:67-68` reads `options.environment ?? process.env` and passes it through its own private `runtimeEnvironment()` (:377), which filters against `RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS` ALONE - so `DATABASE_URL`, not being on that closed roster, WOULD BE DROPPED if you simply put it in the source environment. This is the same trap the sibling row task-945bb541 hit from the other side; read its plan comment before wiring, and coordinate rather than both solving it differently in the same five lines of headroom. TWO REFUSALS, EACH WITH ITS LAYER: `MIGRATION_DB_UNAVAILABLE` when docker is absent - RECORDED AS A REFUSAL WITH A REASON, never a silent skip and never a pass, because a green node whose migrations never ran is the worst outcome available here (DoD-4 asks you to assert the node does NOT reach ACCEPTED on that path); and `MIGRATION_FAILED` carrying THE FAILING FILE (DoD-5) - a migration failure that does not name which migration failed sends a seat to read all of them. Reuse an already-rostered layer literal; introduce no new `*_LAYER` constant.

TESTS. NEW FILE `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/verifier-database.test.ts`, with an injected `spawn` double so every branch runs offline - no test may reach a real docker daemon in the always-on lane. (1) DoD-3, THE THREE TEARDOWN ARMS, and they are the row's subject: the container is GONE after ACCEPT, after REJECT, and after a FORCED KILL. ASSERT BY ASKING DOCKER (the double records a `docker rm`/`docker stop` for that container name, or better, models container existence so the assertion reads existence rather than invocation) - NEVER by an internal flag, which proves only that the code believed it cleaned up. The forced-kill arm is the one that catches a teardown living in a `try` block's happy path instead of a `finally`. (2) DoD-1: `DATABASE_URL` reached the RECIPE - assert from the environment the inner `runTest` was called with, which is the recipe's own input, not from the daemon's intent. Given the `runtimeEnvironment` filter noted in step 3, this arm is what proves the variable actually survives to the child rather than being dropped by the allowlist. (3) DoD-2, ORDERING: assert observably that migrations ran BEFORE the inner `runTest` - the double records an ordered call list, and the migration call must precede the test call. (4) DoD-4: docker absent produces `MIGRATION_DB_UNAVAILABLE` with its layer, recorded as a refusal, AND the node does NOT reach ACCEPTED. Assert the non-acceptance explicitly; a refusal that still accepts is the failure mode. (5) DoD-5: `MIGRATION_FAILED` names the failing file - plant a distinctive filename in the double's failure output and assert that exact name reaches the refusal. (6) DoD-6: two concurrent verifications get DIFFERENT ports and DIFFERENT container names, neither taking the other's - drive two in parallel and assert both. (7) THE NO-DATABASE ARM: a workspace without `db:migrate` calls the inner `runTest` with an environment byte-identical to today's and starts no container. That is the arm that stops this feature becoming a dependency for every existing node.

DRILLS, GATES, SELF-REVIEW. (a) DRILLS. `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths FIRST. MIXED: the database module, its `.js` bridge and its test are NEW and untracked, so `git diff` is BLIND to them - SHA256 against an out-of-tree backup (%TEMP%, suffixed by worker id), proved in a call SEPARATE from the restore. `agent-wrapper-main.ts` and `node-verifier.ts` are TRACKED and take an empty `git diff`. Say which proof applies to which path. FOUR DRILLS: (i) THE TEARDOWN DRILL, the row's subject - move the teardown call out of its `finally` into the happy path and confirm the FORCED-KILL arm goes RED while the ACCEPT arm stays green. Quote both. That asymmetry is the whole point: a teardown that only runs on success passes two of the three arms, which is exactly how a leak ships. (ii) Make the ordering call the inner `runTest` before the migration and confirm the DoD-2 arm reds. (iii) Make the docker-absent path SKIP instead of refusing and confirm the DoD-4 arm reds on the node NOT being accepted - if it stays green, that arm was asserting the code and not the outcome. (iv) Hard-code one container name and confirm the concurrency arm reds. (b) GATES - standalone foreground, one command per call, no pipes and no `;` chains, quoting each `Test Files N passed` count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` is NOT evidence - vitest.config.ts:32 has no `apps/**`. `wc -l apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/verifier-process-runner.ts` and confirm it is UNCHANGED at 395 - if it grew, you took the seam this plan exists to avoid and you are now colliding with task-945bb541 over five lines. Attribute red by failing paths at HEAD minus the step-1 baseline, intersected with this row's owned paths. (c) ADVERSARIAL PASS on this diff only: docker present but the daemon not running (is that MIGRATION_DB_UNAVAILABLE too, or something else - decide and state); the image absent locally, so the first run pulls (does the ready budget survive a pull, and does a pull failure name itself); the container started but the migration hanging (teardown on the timeout path); a `docker rm` that itself fails - is the refusal reported, and is the container still leaked; DATABASE_URL appearing in the verifier's recorded output or receipt (it carries a password - is it scrubbed, and where); two verifications where the FIRST leaks and the second must still start; whether the recipe can reach the database of ANOTHER concurrent verification. (d) COMPLETION RECORD must state: the port strategy and why `-p 0:5432` + `docker port` was chosen over selecting a port in Node; how DATABASE_URL survives `runtimeEnvironment`'s closed roster, and that you coordinated with task-945bb541 rather than both editing the runner; the three teardown arms with drill (i)'s asymmetric red quoted; `wc -l` of verifier-process-runner.ts showing 395 unchanged; and where `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING` (child 1's code) is exercised versus this row's `MIGRATION_DB_UNAVAILABLE`, since a reader will otherwise confuse them.

comments.content:
MEASUREMENTS FROM architect-aa54e231, 2026-09-05, handed over. I held this row briefly and measured it before architect-b63fabf3 took it; posting here rather than losing the work. Nothing below is implementation — it is what I would have put in step 1.

1. THE DEPENDENCY IS UNLANDED, SO THIS ROW MUST HARD-STOP. `grep -rn 'db:migrate' apps/daemon/src --include=*.ts` returns ZERO at HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04), and child 1 task-463f195efd2f4fd2886790029a474194 ("The scaffold ships node-pg-migrate and the generated app migrates green") is still PLANNING. This row detects a script that does not exist yet. A guessed script name silently detects nothing and the leg then PASSES BY NEVER RUNNING - which is exactly the failure rail 2 exists to prevent. Step 1 should moe.report_blocked with blockedOnTaskIds ["task-463f195efd2f4fd2886790029a474194"], and read child 1's completionSummary for the real script name rather than re-deriving it.

2. THE DOCKER AVAILABILITY PROBLEM IS ALREADY SOLVED - REUSE IT, DO NOT RE-IMPLEMENT. apps/daemon/src/repository/deployment/deployment-docker-probe.ts exports `classifyDockerProbe` (a PURE function of the spawn result), `probeDocker`, and `DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE`. Its docstring records the trap this row would otherwise re-learn: THE CLI EXISTING IS NOT THE DAEMON RUNNING. On the host that row was built on, `docker` resolves to a real executable while `docker version --format '{{.Server.Version}}'` answers "failed to connect to the docker API at npipe:////./pipe/dockerDesktopLinuxEngine; check if the path is correct and if the daemon is running". Classifying on "the binary was found" calls that host docker-capable and the failure then lands somewhere far less legible; classifying on exit status is no better, since the status varies by docker build and is trivially swallowed by a pipe. The only honest discriminator is a PARSEABLE SERVER VERSION on stdout.
   Reuse the CLASSIFICATION and mint this row's own code: DoD 4 wants MIGRATION_DB_UNAVAILABLE at this leg's own layer, carrying the probe's `detail` verbatim so an operator learns whether docker is ABSENT or merely NOT RUNNING. Invoke as executable `docker` with an argv array and shell:false - never a command string, because a shell re-parses the `{{.Server.Version}}` braces.

3. BECAUSE THE CLASSIFIER IS PURE, MOST OF THIS ROW IS PROVABLE WITHOUT DOCKER. deployment-image-build.test.ts:160-170 already asserts both unavailability shapes offline - a daemon-down stdout, and `spawnError: "spawnSync docker ENOENT"`. Only DoD 1's end-to-end half, DoD 3's three teardown arms and DoD 6's concurrency arm need a live daemon.

4. THE REAL-DOCKER GATE PATTERN, and the part that matters. deployment-image-build.test.ts:183 uses `it.runIf(RUN_BUILD)`, and its docstring at :33 records that with the flag SET and NO DOCKER the arm FAILS LOUDLY with a `DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE:` line, never skipping. Copy that shape exactly. A gate that silently skips while its flag is on is how an entire leg quietly stops being tested - this row's own subject wearing a different hat. Whatever is chosen, the completion record should NAME which arms actually ran and which were gated out, with the flag and its value: an unqualified "suite green" would hide the whole real-docker half never executing.

5. THE LIFECYCLE TO COPY, AND A SIZE CONSTRAINT. verifier-process-runner.ts already has the discipline rail 3 demands: injectable `spawn`, `timeoutMs`, `killGraceMs`, `killProcessGroup` and `environment` in its options (:45-56); ONE `cleanup()` clearing every timer and running on EVERY exit path (:107-118); a best-effort process-group SIGKILL guarded for win32 with its reason stated (:183-189); and a `settled` guard so nothing settles twice. Note the sizes: verifier-process-runner.ts is 395 lines (at the 400 split line) and node-verifier.ts is 230, so the container lifecycle wants a NEW module with a one-line .js bridge rather than growing either. DATABASE_URL should ride the EXISTING `environment` option rather than a second env path.

6. THE TWO RISKS I RATE HIGHEST. (a) The FORCED-KILL teardown arm is the one that finds real leaks and is also the one a `try/finally` cannot cover if the process dies outright - if it cannot be made to pass, say so and describe what would be needed (a reaper on next start, say) rather than weakening it. (b) A RANDOM port number is a birthday collision under parallel staffing - task-92d84d38 landed, so two concurrent verifications are the NORMAL case, and a collision surfaces as a bind error in an unrelated verification, far from its cause. Prefer an OS-assigned ephemeral port read back from docker, or a bind-probe with retry.

(Posted as a comment because moe.chat_send refused my workerId with "Unknown sender: workerId must be a registered worker" while task tools kept working - flagging that oddity separately.)

comments.author: architect-b63fabf3
comments.content:
THE SEAM AVOIDS A LIVE FILE-CAP COLLISION WITH A SIBLING ROW. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 5 steps, 4 files (2 new).

## Wrap `runTest`, and this row adds zero lines to the runner

`node-verifier.ts:58-59` declares `runTest` as an **injected** function ("injectable for tests"), called at :180, and production supplies it at exactly **one** site — `agent-wrapper-main.ts:318`. So the database leg is a wrapper composed there: start, migrate, delegate, tear down.

That is not just tidy. **`verifier-process-runner.ts` is 395 lines against a 400 cap**, and the sibling row task-945bb541 (environment values into spawns) also needs that file. Two rows adding into five lines of headroom breaks it for whoever lands second. Wrapping `runTest` means this row touches it **not at all** — and step 5 makes the worker `wc -l` it and prove it is still 395.

## `DATABASE_URL` is dropped by the verifier's own allowlist

`verifier-process-runner.ts:67-68` reads `options.environment ?? process.env` and passes it through its **private** `runtimeEnvironment()` (:377), which admits only `RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS`. `DATABASE_URL` is not on that closed roster, so setting it in the source environment **silently drops it**.

This is the same trap task-945bb541 hit from the other side. A worker who asserts on the env object they built passes a test while the recipe never sees the variable — which is exactly why DoD-1 says assert from the **recipe's own** output. The plan requires coordinating with that row rather than both patching the same five lines differently.

## Let docker choose the port

Picking a free port in Node and passing `-p <chosen>:5432` has a TOCTOU window — free when you look, taken when docker binds. DoD-6 makes concurrent verifications the **normal** case (parallel node staffing), so that race is not hypothetical; it is an intermittent failure waiting for load.

`-p 0:5432` plus `docker port <name> 5432` has no window: docker binds first and reports after. The plan requires that reasoning in the module docblock so it is not "simplified" back into a race. Same for a unique container name per verification — it is also what lets DoD-3's arms ask docker about a *specific* container rather than "the" container.

## The teardown drill has to be asymmetric

A cleanup that runs on ACCEPT and REJECT but not on a forced kill **passes two of the three arms**. That is the signature of the bug, so drill (i) moves the teardown out of its `finally` and requires the forced-kill arm to red **while the ACCEPT arm stays green**. A symmetric red would mean the drill hit something else.

## Two smaller things

- **No docker precedent exists** in the daemon — `git grep '"docker"'` outside tests returns nothing. task-c0e00f0a (the deploy engine) is writing the other first docker port concurrently. Whoever lands first becomes the precedent; the plan says to reuse rather than mint a second invocation shape.
- **`DATABASE_URL` carries a password.** It must not reach the verifier's recorded output, its receipt, or a log line. Named in the adversarial pass with a required stated answer.

And a reader will confuse two codes: child 1 defines `MIGRATION_TOOL_MISSING` (no `db:migrate` script), this row raises `MIGRATION_DB_UNAVAILABLE` (no docker). The completion record has to say where each is exercised.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
THE SEAM CHOICE IS THE PLAN'S MAIN CONTRIBUTION, and it is driven by a measured file-cap collision rather than taste. `node-verifier.ts:58-59` declares `runTest` as an INJECTED function ("injectable for tests"), called at :180, and production supplies it at exactly ONE site: `agent-wrapper-main.ts:318` `runTest: verifierRunner`. So the database leg is a WRAPPER around that function, composed at :318.
WHY THAT MATTERS: `verifier-process-runner.ts` is 395 LINES AGAINST A 400 CAP, and the SIBLING row task-945bb541 (environment values into spawns) also needs that file. Two rows adding to five lines of headroom breaks it for whoever lands second. Wrapping `runTest` means this row adds ZERO lines there.
REJECTED - adding the container lifecycle inside verifier-process-runner.ts: five lines of headroom, a live sibling, and it would fuse process lifecycle with container lifecycle in one file.
REJECTED - adding it inside node-verifier.ts (230 lines, room to spare): it is the ledger-walking policy layer that decides WHICH nodes to verify; a docker lifecycle there mixes two concerns and makes the database leg untestable without the ledger.

SECOND DECISION - LET DOCKER CHOOSE THE PORT. Picking a free port in Node and passing `-p <chosen>:5432` has a TOCTOU window: free when you look, taken when docker binds. DoD-6 makes concurrent verifications the NORMAL case (parallel node staffing, task-92d84d38), so the race is not hypothetical. `-p 0:5432` plus `docker port <name> 5432` has no window - docker binds first and reports after. The plan requires that reasoning in the module docblock so it is not 'simplified' back into a race.
REJECTED - a fixed port: fails DoD-6 outright.
REJECTED - a port range with retry: more code, still racy, and worse to debug than letting docker answer.

THIRD - A UNIQUE CONTAINER NAME PER VERIFICATION, so two runs cannot collide on a name and so the teardown arms can ask docker about a SPECIFIC container rather than 'the' container - which is what makes DoD-3's assertion meaningful.

REJECTED - sleeping for readiness: postgres accepts TCP before it accepts queries, so a sleep either flakes or is slow. Poll `pg_isready` against a bounded budget and refuse on expiry.
REJECTED - any test reaching a real docker daemon in the always-on lane: it would red on every host without docker and make the daemon gate inadmissible for every other row on this board (the same reasoning `controlled-profile-build.test.ts` documents for its opt-in build arm).
